title: Pongal: The Four Days of Tamil Nadu's Harvest Festival

content: Pongal is a harvest festival celebrated in January, marking the end of the winter harvest season and giving thanks to the Sun and to farming communities.

It is observed over four days: Bhogi, when old items are discarded; Thai Pongal, the main day on which rice is boiled with milk until it overflows; Mattu Pongal, which honours cattle; and Kaanum Pongal, a day for family gatherings and outings.
Local customs vary between families and regions, but the shared themes of gratitude, new beginnings and community remain.
